import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 188

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/188](https://www.erdosproblems.com/188)
- [EGMRSS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Montgomery, P. and Rothschild, B. L. and Spencer, J.
  and Straus, E. G., Euclidean {R}amsey theorems. {II}. (1975), 529--557.
- [Ts17] Tsaturian, Sergei, A {E}uclidean {R}amsey result in the plane. Electron. J. Combin. (2017),
  Paper No. 4.35, 9.
-/

namespace Erdos188

/--
The set of numbers $k$ such that $\mathbb{R}^2$ can be red/blue coloured with no pair of red
points unit distance apart, and no $k$-term arithmetic progression of blue points with distance 1.
-/
def s := { k : ℕ | ∃ blue : Set ℂ,
  (Set.univ \ blue).Pairwise (fun c₁ c₂ => dist c₁ c₂ ≠ 1) ∧
    ¬ (∃ᵉ (bs ⊆ blue) (z) (d), ‖d‖ = 1 ∧ bs.IsAPOfLengthWith k z d) }

/--
What is the smallest $k$ such that $\mathbb{R}^2$ can be red/blue coloured with no pair of red
points unit distance apart, and no $k$-term arithmetic progression of blue points with distance 1?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_188 : IsLeast s answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory by Erdős & Graham (Page 14, 15):

It has been shown that there is a large $M$ so that it is possible to partition $\mathbb{E}^2$ into
two sets $A$ and $B$ so that $A$ contains no pair of points with distance 1 and $B$ contains no A.P.
of length $M$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_188.variants.nonempty : s.Nonempty := by
  sorry

/--
Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory by Erdős & Graham (Page 15):

How small can $M$ be made? The only estimate currently known is that $M \le 10000000$ (more or less).
In the other direction, it has just been shown by R. Juhász [Ju (79)] that we must have $M \ge 5$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_188.variants.estimate : (∀ k, k ∈ s → 5 ≤ k) ∧ (∃ k ∈ s, k ≤ 10000000) := by
  sorry

end Erdos188

reformulations.difference: The Lean uses subsets of ℂ and a finite-set arithmetic-progression predicate rather than an explicit red/blue colouring of the Euclidean plane and congruent copies of the unit-spaced configuration ℓ_k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Complex.orthonormalBasisOneI.repr is a real linear isometric equivalence from ℂ to EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), preserving distances and progressions. A blue set and its complement encode the two colours. When ‖d‖ = 1, d ≠ 0 and n ↦ z + n • d is injective, so its first k terms have cardinality exactly k. Consequently the existential bs condition is equivalent to all those terms being blue. I proved the complete membership equivalence with the Euclidean-plane formulation in Review188.mem_s_iff_euclidean_plane, without using the problem's sorry-backed theorems.

reformulations.difference: The bounds are expressed as a lower bound on every feasible k and the existence of a feasible k below the upper bound, rather than as inequalities for the smallest feasible value.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If m is the least element of s, then (∀ k ∈ s, 5 ≤ k) is equivalent to 5 ≤ m: evaluate at m in one direction and use m ≤ k in the other. Likewise, (∃ k ∈ s, k ≤ 10000000) is equivalent to m ≤ 10000000: use minimality in one direction and choose k = m in the other. This equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf — Erdős–Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory, pp. 14–15.
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-07.pdf — Erdős–Graham, earlier article version, pp. 330–331.

review.notes:
Checked all four declarations, the answer's natural-number type, quantifier scopes, and the underlying definitions. Lean tests establish 0,1 ∉ s, the AP cases of lengths 0, 1 and 2, failure of either monochromatic colouring, and upward closure of s. IsLeast includes membership and therefore genuinely constrains the answer.

The current website explicitly explains that Erdős–Graham omitted the unit-step restriction in their original wording and interprets the intended problem with that restriction. The file follows this corrected formulation; the historical quotations should be read in that context. The website describes the 10^7 upper bound as a claim made 'more or less', without a supplied proof. The estimate reproduces that reported inequality; this review does not independently certify its proof status. Tsaturian's stronger lower bound does not invalidate the historical lower bound 5. The main problem's open tag agrees with the source.
